source: Minchat Shai on Lev 4:34 (Zevachim 37b-38a; Rashi; the Ramah; the Meiri; Shemen Sasson; Ramban responsum 232)
claim_en: The horn-word dispute: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel both read the three outer-altar sin-offering passages (the ruler 4:25, the she-goat 4:30, the lamb 4:34) on the premise that ONE of them writes qarnot ('horns') FULL. MS rules: 'ALL the books and their Masorah lists agree — all three are LEAN, not one full... and wherever the Talmud disputes the Masorah on lean-and-full we follow the Masorah, even where law hangs on it.' SNAPSHOT sides with the Masorah: every qarnot of the chapter's dispute-stations lean — five lean tokens in the Torah, the three of the dispute among them.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

claim_en: 'He shall bring the bull to the door of the tent of meeting BEFORE the LORD' — the scribes' conjecture (sevirin) expects asher lifne ('WHICH is before the LORD'); the verse writes no asher at all. The rejected-conjecture class; the list's partner is Solomon's bronze altar (2 Chr 1:5-6, outside the Torah instrument).

claim_en: 'And the priest shall dip HIS FINGER' — some err and recite et here, says MS: the FIRST passage (4:6) writes 'et his-finger', this one writes the finger WITHOUT et. Verified structurally: this is the ONLY place in the Torah where ha-kohen ('the priest') is directly followed by etzbao ('his finger').
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)
